response.question: Give the complete ordered method for ordinary Harbor docket worksheets with no seal.
response.answer:
Source extracts (not model-generated):

Do not skip the approval check. The following complete procedure applies to ordinary worksheets with no seal. 1. Verify the signed supervisor approval before starting the Harbor docket transfer. Check that the approval names the docket identifier and the current operating date, and place the approval beside the register. 2. Copy the docket identifier onto the transfer register. Copy the receiving desk, the dispatch date, and the operator initials onto the same register row so the transfer can be traced during the handover. 3. Compare the register total with the docket total. Count every listed envelope, compare each envelope identifier with the dispatch list, and record the checked count beside the register total before moving the envelopes. 4. Place the checked envelopes in the transfer basket. Arrange the envelopes in dispatch list order, attach the register copy to the basket handle, and leave the original dispatch list on the supervisor desk. 5. Carry the transfer basket to the receiving desk. Ask the receiving clerk to compare the basket count with the register copy and to initial the count field while the basket remains on the desk. 6. Record the receiving clerk initials in the original register. Record the handover time beside the initials, confirm that the receiving desk has the register copy, and retain the original register for the closure check. 7. Compare the completed register with the supervisor approval. Confirm that the docket identifier, envelope count, receiving clerk initials, and handover time are all present, and obtain the supervisor closure signature on the final line. 8. Close the transfer register and place the completed docket in the archive tray. Lock the archive tray, return the archive key to the supervisor, and end the transfer only after the supervisor records receipt of the key. Do not reopen the transfer after closure. [1]

procedure_completeness.source_body: This is a Harbor docket worksheet convention. Do not skip the approval check. The following complete procedure applies to ordinary worksheets with no seal. 1. Verify the signed supervisor approval before starting the Harbor docket transfer. Check that the approval names the docket identifier and the current operating date, and place the approval beside the register. 2. Copy the docket identifier onto the transfer register. Copy the receiving desk, the dispatch date, and the operator initials onto the same register row so the transfer can be traced during the handover. 3. Compare the register total with the docket total. Count every listed envelope, compare each envelope identifier with the dispatch list, and record the checked count beside the register total before moving the envelopes. 4. Place the checked envelopes in the transfer basket. Arrange the envelopes in dispatch list order, attach the register copy to the basket handle, and leave the original dispatch list on the supervisor desk. 5. Carry the transfer basket to the receiving desk. Ask the receiving clerk to compare the basket count with the register copy and to initial the count field while the basket remains on the desk. 6. Record the receiving clerk initials in the original register. Record the handover time beside the initials, confirm that the receiving desk has the register copy, and retain the original register for the closure check. 7. Compare the completed register with the supervisor approval. Confirm that the docket identifier, envelope count, receiving clerk initials, and handover time are all present, and obtain the supervisor closure signature on the final line. 8. Close the transfer register and place the completed docket in the archive tray. Lock the archive tray, return the archive key to the supervisor, and end the transfer only after the supervisor records receipt of the key. Do not reopen the transfer after closure.

procedure_completeness.source_body: This is a Harbor docket worksheet convention. Do not skip the approval check. The following complete procedure applies to ordinary worksheets with no seal. 1. Verify the signed supervisor approval before starting the Harbor docket transfer. Check that the approval names the docket identifier and the current operating date, and place the approval beside the register. 2. Copy the docket identifier onto the transfer register. Copy the receiving desk, the dispatch date, and the operator initials onto the same register row so the transfer can be traced during the handover. 3. Compare the register total with the docket total. Count every listed envelope, compare each envelope identifier with the dispatch list, and record the checked count beside the register total before moving the envelopes. 4. Place the checked envelopes in the transfer basket. Arrange the envelopes in dispatch list order, attach the register copy to the basket handle, and leave the original dispatch list on the supervisor desk. 5. Carry the transfer basket to the receiving desk. Ask the receiving clerk to compare the basket count with the register copy and to initial the count field while the basket remains on the desk. 6. Record the receiving clerk initials in the original register. Record the handover time beside the initials, confirm that the receiving desk has the register copy, and retain the original register for the closure check. 7. Compare the completed register with the supervisor approval. Confirm that the docket identifier, envelope count, receiving clerk initials, and handover time are all present, and obtain the supervisor closure signature on the final line. 8. Close the transfer register and place the completed docket in the archive tray. Lock the archive tray, return the archive key to the supervisor, and end the transfer only after the supervisor records receipt of the key. Do not reopen the transfer after closure.

bea0eb53-0dbd-4526-bd55-ede37aed6d5e.body: This is a Harbor docket worksheet convention. Do not skip the approval check. The following complete procedure applies to ordinary worksheets with no seal. 1. Verify the signed supervisor approval before starting the Harbor docket transfer. Check that the approval names the docket identifier and the current operating date, and place the approval beside the register. 2. Copy the docket identifier onto the transfer register. Copy the receiving desk, the dispatch date, and the operator initials onto the same register row so the transfer can be traced during the handover. 3. Compare the register total with the docket total. Count every listed envelope, compare each envelope identifier with the dispatch list, and record the checked count beside the register total before moving the envelopes. 4. Place the checked envelopes in the transfer basket. Arrange the envelopes in dispatch list order, attach the register copy to the basket handle, and leave the original dispatch list on the supervisor desk. 5. Carry the transfer basket to the receiving desk. Ask the receiving clerk to compare the basket count with the register copy and to initial the count field while the basket remains on the desk. 6. Record the receiving clerk initials in the original register. Record the handover time beside the initials, confirm that the receiving desk has the register copy, and retain the original register for the closure check. 7. Compare the completed register with the supervisor approval. Confirm that the docket identifier, envelope count, receiving clerk initials, and handover time are all present, and obtain the supervisor closure signature on the final line. 8. Close the transfer register and place the completed docket in the archive tray. Lock the archive tray, return the archive key to the supervisor, and end the transfer only after the supervisor records receipt of the key. Do not reopen the transfer after closure.
